An informant called to report an abandoned tent and equipment. The owner of the equipment had already informed the team of it's location and the circumstances.The team leader confirmed the location and that it was the same equipment and closed the job with no team deployment - park authorities were informed.

An individual had fallen approximately 6m  in the Penmaenbach quarries and suffered a badly broken ankle. The team were deployed and once on scene and the casualty assessed, it was decided that an expedient extraction by helicopter would be required. Rescue 336 was tasked and was able to lift the casualty for direct transfer to hospital.

A walker attempting part of the Welsh 3000s was reported as overdue by a family member who was expecting them in Nant Peris. Last contact had been at approximately 6pm when the walker was descending Glyder Fawr. OVMRO initially took the call but then handed it over to LLMRT as it was more likely the walker would be in their area. An Oggie TL managed briefly to speak with the overdue walker who stated they were ok and did not need assistance. Shortly afterwards they arrived at Nant Peris safe and well and both teams stood down.
Party on the hill pocket dialled the police but then went out of signal.  The team leader was able to contact the caller and there were no issues so the job was closed with no further action.

Two people were swimming in the Afon Conwy near Fairy Glen when one got into difficulties. Their friend called 999 and a multi-agency response was instigated with team members arriving on scene as HEMS and WAST staff were attending to the casualty. MR assistance was not required for the extraction so team members were stood down shortly after.

A group of three were bouldering in the Tubes area of the Afon Conwy, downstream of the Conwy Falls when one took a 7m fall and sustained an injury to their spine. Their friends called 999 and local team members were directed to the incident site on the south side of the river, they were able to access the cas site and begin assessment. Further team members collected medical and rope rescue kit from base. A full technical rope rescue system was established and the casualty, packaged into a stretcher, was lifted out of the gorge and up to the roadside where they were transferred to an ambulance for onward transport to hospital.

A walker was ascending the east ridge of Y Garn when they heard a cry for help so rang North Wales Police. The team leader spoke with informant who had ascended the Devil's Kitchen and was near a body of water. After further investigation it was established that the informant had heard no further cries for help and had no response to their shouts. The team leader confirmed with NWP that no further reports had been made in the area and no further action was taken.

A group were scrambling on the north ridge of Tryfan when one of their party sustained a series of deep leg abrasions to both legs.  Team members were deployed as a hasty party and Rescue 336 was tasked.  The casualty location was just at cloud level but the winch-paramedic was lowered onto the casualty's location and began assessment. The casualty was packaged into a stretcher and lifted directly to hospital.

Two walkers reported they were stuck on the summit of Tryfan because their torches had failed and they could not see to descend. As the call came in at 03:30 the team leader suggested that if they waited an hour it would be full daylight, with no other injuries or concerns a that time time, the team were not immediately deployed. The walker's phones had limited battery power so the next communication was at 08:30 once they had walked back to the road, to report they were safe and well.

location_text: Pen yr Ole Wen, south ridge
narrative_raw: Two walkers found an unattended rucksack on the path down from Pen yr Ole Wen down to the Ogwen Cottage on the A5. There was no-one in the vicinity and it was dusk so they had a quick check of the contents to search for any ID and got the impression it may have been there for some time. North Wales Police reported the rucksack to OVMRO. The team leader spoke with the informant and agreed that there was no further action required unless NWP get a report of a missing/overdue person.

An individual was walking by the river close to the Miner's Bridge in Betws y Coed when they slipped and sustained an ankle injury. WAST took the first call and were able to reach  and treat the casualty but could not extract them over the rocky river bed. The team were asked to help so a small party attended with a stretcher for a short extraction back to the road and waiting ambulance.

The team doctor had just finished assisting the previous casualty (O110628) when another by-passer asked for assistance for an individual who had a possible sprained ankle at the bottom of the Bochlwyd steps. The team doctor examined the injury, gave the casualty some pain relief and then assisted the casualty down the hill to the roadside with the intention to self-present at hospital.

A scrambler took a tumbling fall of about 20 metres on rough ground suffering injuries to their neck, ankle and wrist. Another climber close to the incident rang 999 for help and team members deployed on foot to site and due to the possible serious nature of the injuries the rescue helicopter R336 was deployed. The winch-paramedic was dropped on scene and the hill team helped package the casualty into a vacmat and stretcher to be winched off and flown directly to hospital

A solo scrambler on Daear Ddu lost the route near the summit area and requested assistance to get out of steep terrain. The hot weather and the use of a paper map, with the summit area of Moel Siabod at the join, made it difficult for the person to follow the scramble. As the team was gathering at base, the individual called to say they had reached the summit and was happy to make their own way down to the road so no deployment was required.

An individual was reported to have disappeared into the water while paddleboarding with a group at Llyn Geirionydd. The team responded alongside North Wales Police, Fire and Rescue Services and Welsh Ambulance Service. The team conducted bankside searches and shallow water raft searches whilst waiting for the fire service powered boat to begin deeper water searches. The individual was located by the boat team and further operations were passed over to the police divers. The team's thoughts are with the family and friends of the casualty.

An informant was passing Llyn ogwen when they saw people climbing a rock face near the lake and heard shouts. They tried calling to them to make sure they were ok but did not receive a reply so called to report. The team leader spoke with informant and after ensuring no other calls had been made explained that the are was a popular spot with rock climbers. No further action was taken.

An individual had been reported as missing from home with concern for their wellbeing. North Wales Police requested support in searching Penmaenmawr quarries but shortly after initial enquiries the individual was found by police in their vehicle and no further action was required.

A solo walker lost the path near the summit of Tryfan and asked for advice on a route down. The team leader used Phonefind to ascertain their position and was then able to guide them back towards safe ground and the main descent path. Once back on the track and confident they needed no further help, the job was closed and no deployment was required.
Ongoing support to North Wales Police for the missing person search. Team leadership attended NWP Silver meeting to assist with tasking for NPAS fixed wing aircraft for search areas in the afternoon.

A solo walker lost the path whist descending the North Ridge of Tryfan and called for assistance. Three team members deployed in heavy rain to locate the individual who was found on relatively safe ground, rewarmed and assisted back to the main path and down to the roadside.

A solo walker was reported missing by their family, having left home on Thursday, 25 June. The walker's vehicle was located in Nant Francon with a note stating their intended route taking in Carnedd y Filiast. Initial searches made use of multiple search resources including team members, Rescue 912 from Humberside, Rescue 336, RAFMRT and SARDA(Wales) dogs. Search effort was suspended at about 21:00 after a hot day with high winds and cloud impacting the search effort on the high elevations.

A young person fell into the Afon Ogwen at Ogwen Bank and sustained various injuries. They were pulled out but WAST requested assistance to move them to the ambulance. Team members arrived on scene after the paramedics had managed to move the casualty up to the ambulance so no further action was required.

An informant called to report two climbers who were overdue returning from a climbing excursion on Ysgolion Duon (Black Ladders). No other information was available and not contact could be made with the pair so a small hill team was deployed to walk in from Gerlan to investigate. The Coastguard helicopter was also tasked to begin an initial search. Shortly after the climbers arrived back at the vehicle and made contact - team members and the aircraft were stood down.

The team was called to help coordinate and possibly assist with a report of a suspected EOD device found on Glyder Fach. The incident was handed over to RAFMRT liaised directly with the EOD team with no further OVMRO involvement or deployment.

Two walkers were in the area of Glyder Fach but got lost and called for assistance after becoming cold and wet. The Team Leader was able to make phone contact with the pair initially and guide them down using Phonefind/Sarloc. No team deployment was required.

Two walkers were attempting to descend the East Face of Tryfan but strayed into very steep ground and one of the pair slipped a short distance down a gulley and hurt their head. Their partner was stuck on a ledge several metres above so called for help. A hill party was deployed and shortly after the informant called again to say they had managed to self-extract down to the heather terrace path. The pair began to walk off slowly and were met by the hill party, the casualty was assessed, the wound dressed, and they were assisted back to base before self-presenting at hospital.

A par were scrambling on the North Ridge of Tryfan when one banged their head on the underside of a protruding rock, the laceration initially bled significantly and they began to feel dizzy so called for assistance. The team leader spoke with the informant by which time they had dressed the wound and the casualty was feeling a little better so they were advised to start descending to the road and a hill party would walk up to meet them. They made very good progress and the team members met up with them close to Milestone Buttress. The casualty was assessed and advised to self-present at hospital to have the wound examined.

Two people reported themselves lost in the Devil's Kitchen area. Phone signal dropped out before contact details or location confirmed was confirmed so OVMRO team members responded to base. Shortly after, the walkers had sent an SOS signal via their phone and it was established they were in the Afon Gafr area above Nant Peris. The incident was transferred to LLMRT and OVMRO stood down with no further involvement.

A person was scrambling along the Eastern Traverse of Tryfan with their dog when the dog had a small slip and then became frightened by the high winds and refused to move. A small team was deployed from Oggi Base to reach the walker and dog and, using a dog harness, assisted the owner in getting the dog back on to reasonable ground and out of the worse of the wind before descending back down to the roadside.

A party were descending past Twll Ddu when one of the group took a 3m fall and sustained a head injury. A small hill party, having just finished an earlier job, was deployed as a hasty party to locate and assess the casualty with additional team members following up with additional stretcher equipment. The casualty was assessed and, given the location and their level of mobility, were assisted in descending the steep ground with short-rope protection before walking down to Ogwen Cottage. The group attended base for refreshment before self-presenting at hospital.

Welsh Ambulance Service (WAST) requested assistance with extraction of a mountain biker who had sustained a knee injury in the Gwydyr Forest. A hill team were deployed with stretcher equipment and extracted the casualty back to the road to be transferred to the ambulance.

North Wales Police received multiple reports of flares sighted in the northern Carneddau. After a short investigation it was established that the RAF MRT were training in the area and no further action was required.

An informant walking in the vicinity of Idwal slabs heard a shout and saw something/someone falling. Concerned that this was a fallen climber they reported to the police and spoke with the team leader. With further investigation the most likely cause was a dropped rucksack. Multiple parties on Idwal slabs had seen a pair abseil to the location of the falling item. No climbers in the area were panicked and no other calls as had been received so the incident was closed with no further action and no deployment.

An individual was reported to have injured their ankle on the North Ridge path of Tryfan, near Milestone Buttress. The team responded and a hasty party was dispatched to access, and assess the inured person while further team members followed with stretcher equipment. The casualty initially tried to mobilise down with assistance but the pain was too much so they were placed on to the stretcher and extracted down to the A5 and transferred to their own vehicle to self-present at hospital.

A family group were visiting Aber falls when one of the party slipped and fell approximately 4-5m over rocks sustaining painful injuries to arms and legs. Due to poor phone signal in the area it was difficult to call for help but eventually the team were called with local team members attending directly and others deploying from base. An aircraft was also requested because of episodes of unconsciousness.  On arrival team members found the individual had self-mobilised with the assistance of passers-by and walked some distance down the track. After assessment and further examination by a WAST paramedic, the casualty was transported directly to hospital by team vehicle with RRV support.

A group were scrambling up Bristly Ridge and after they passed the top pinnacle one of the party was hit by a falling rock and sustained an injury to their upper arm. A hill team was deployed ahead of a SAR helicopter becoming available. As the the hill team approached the back-wall of Cwm Tryfan, the aircraft arrived on scene. They were able to drop a winch-paramedic close to the casualty for assessment before returning to winch them and transfer directly to hospital.

The welsh ambulance service requested help with accessing and extracting an individual from Llanddygai viaduct, Bangor. Local team members attended directly and assisted NWFRS in transferring the individual to a nearby ambulance.

North Wales Police requested assistance with a search for a missing person. The initial request was for OVMRO to link across to SARDA Wales for an air scenting dog support. Once NWP was contacted the individual had been found, but in a difficult-to-access location. The team remained on standby to support HM Coastguard evacuate the person but no deployment was required.

An informant called with concern regarding shouts for help in the area of the west face of Tryfan. When the team leader followed up they established that there had been no further shouts or responses to calls, no additional reports to the police and that there were goats in the area. No further action was taken.

An informant called to report their friend had slipped and injured their ankle and was unable to continue. Initially this was thought to be in OVMRO but SARLOC placed the casualty on Yr Wyddfa. The job was passed to LLMRT with OVMRO remaining on standby to assist as Llanberis were dealing with 5 concurrent jobs though no OVMRO assistance was eventually required.

Two climbers called to inform that they were assisting two other climbers on descent from gashed crag. The team were placed on standby in the event that full technical rope rescue was required but the informants were able to enact the rescue and the group were monitored remotely back to the roadside with no OVMRO deployment.

Two walkers called to request assistance when they became stuck on the descent of Tryfan north ridge and were getting cold. A small hill party was deployed to locate the pair who were in the area of the west face. The team climbed up to the north ridge via western gully and then north down the ridge to the walkers' location. After warming up the pair with jackets and hot drinks, they were short-roped back along the ridge to western gully and then down to the roadside and back to their vehicle.
The team received a call for assistance with a walker who had slipped and suffered back injuries on the Nantlle Ridge. The job was passed on to Aberglaslyn MRT with no further Ogwen involvement.

A walker became stuck on the upper part of Bristly Ridge when they became separated a short distance from the rest of their group. Two RAF MRT parties were close by and volunteered to assist while Oggie remained on standby. The RAFMRT were able to locate the walker and short-roped them to safe ground before assisting them back to the roadside. No OVMRO deployment was required.

A walker slipped on the descent of the south ridge of Tryfan and injured their ankle, unable to continue on, their friend called for assistance. A hasty party arrived on scene shortly before the Coastguard helicopter from St Athan. A stretcher party had also been deployed but waited at Bochlwyd outflow while the casualty was winched into the helicopter and flown to Oggie Base. All team members returned to base and the casualty plus friend were advised to attend the local hospital for further assessment.

A party of three walkers began to descend off Glyder Fach but became cragfast in steep ground to the side of main face. A large hill party was deployed to locate the group. Team members approached from below and climbed the gulley in order to get in above the walkers. A technical rope rescue system was established to extract the group back to safe ground and then they were assisted back down to the roadside.

A lone walker had left Capel Curig early in the morning and walked the ridge line to the Miner's track and then up Tryfan the south ridge. While descending they strayed into steep ground on the east face until they were unable to continue on or back, so called for help. A hill party was deployed up the North Ridge and onto the Eastern Traverse, they were able to lower a team to the walker's location and established a scrambling route down to the heather terrace path before descending to base.

While walking alongside Llyn Cowlyd a lone hill walker slipped and fell onto their hand sustaining a painful injury. Direct communication and location of the casualty was not possible so two hill parties were deployed to either end of the lake. Local team members met with the walker who had self-extracted to the dam. The injury was assessed and splinted and the walker was assisted to hospital.

An informant called with concern for an overdue couple who were last known to be in the Devil's Kitchen area. Whilst the duty team leader was gathering further information the absent walker's called to report their safety and whereabouts. The job was closed with no further action or deployment.

A party of two went walking in the Tryfan area but with no navigation equipment or knowledge of the area decided to follow some other walkers and eventually became stuck in steep ground. They called for help and the team leader was able to locate the pair who were fortunately near a path. The TL was able to instruct the walkers by phone and guide them back down to the A5. No hill deployment was required.

Two climbers had ascended Idwal Buttress and were continuing on to the grey slabs area of Glyder Fawr but soon realised they were off route and unable to continue up or down so called for assistance. Team members gathered at base to deploy and given the location the coastguard helicopter was also requested. The aircraft was able to access the pair and winch them directly from the crag before dropping them down at Oggie Base.

Welsh Ambulance Service (WAS) paramedics requested assistance with moving an individual who had slipped and injured their leg while visiting Dolwyddelan castle. The casualty was assessed and treated by the paramedics and OVMRO team members deployed with stretcher equipment to extract the casualty down to the roadside and into the ambulance.

An informant called to request help with one of their group who had slipped and painfully injured their ankle while walking in Cwm Idwal. Two of their party descended to the visitor's centre and guided team members back to the cas location. The casualty was assessed and the limb splinted while additional team members arrived with stretcher equipment. The injured walker was extracted down to the visitor's centre with the intention to self-present at hospital.

An informant reported two friends who had called them to say they were on the Carneddau but were lost and cold in bad weather. It was not possible to gain direct communications with the walkers so two teams were deployed from base to sweep the main ridge area from Cefn Ysgolion Duon to Carnedd Llewelyn and another from Cwm Llygwy up to Carned Llewelyn. Another party of walkers came across the pair and called to inform they were assisting them down (job O054842). The group were met by the second hill team who took them down to Ogwen Base.

A solo scrambler became crag fast on Idwal slabs in the area of tennis shoe route. A hasty party was deployed to assess and locate the individual who was assisted by nearby climbers. Team members remained on standby until the scrambler was confirmed back at the visitor's centre.
The team received a call for an incident on the PyG track on Yr Wyddfa. Thea team leader passed this on to Llanberis MRT who were already aware. No OVMRO deployment was required.

An informant called to say their friend had slipped on the coastal path and had badly injured their ankle. The cas was located and a hill party deployed to assess and begin cas care. Once packaged for a stretcher extraction the cas was transported to a waiting team vehicle and then directly on to hospital.

A walker called to say they had slipped while descending Glyder fawr and injured, possible breaking, their ankle and were unable to continue. The team were called out but due to the location the Coastguard helicopter was also requested and tasked. The helicopter was able to access and winch the casualty directly to hospital while their partner was happy to descend alone.

An informant called with concern for a family member who had reported lost on Tryfan, with a snapchat pin placing them on the east face, but had been uncontactable for about 90 minutes. Following initial enquiries team vehicles were deployed to try and spot the walkers who were soon located at Ogwen Cottage.

A walker became separated from their friends on the ascent of Tryfan but lost the path and was stuck in steep ground. Sarloc placed the walker in the area of Nor Nor gulley. A hasty party was deployed with warm clothing while a second team deployed with additional rope equipment. The walker was located on steep grassy terrain and it was possible to extract them with short-rope before descending back to the roadside. Their friends were located at Ogwen Cottage and reunited at Ogwen Base.

Two walkers became lost in the cloud and darkness somewhere on the Carneddau so called for assistance. Without a smartphone it was not possible to ascertain a location through Sarloc but the walkers had a map and believed they were in the area of Afon Caseg. A small hill party were initially deployed but were unable to locate the pair so the Coastguard helicopter was tasked to assist. The helicopter located the pair near to Afon Goch above Aber Falls but could not extract due to low cloud. A hill party deployed to rendezvous with the pair and assist them off the hill.

Two walkers were stuck in steep ground above the milestone buttress area of Tryfan. An initial hasty party were deployed to locate the pair and secure their location while further team members followed up with additional equipment. Safety lines were rigged to assist the pair onto safe ground before walking them back down to the roadside.
An informant called with concern for others intending to camp in the Devil's Kitchen area. The team leader spoke with the informant and North Wales Police and no further action was required.

Two walkers called for assistance as they had lost the path whilst descending into Devil's Kitchen/Twll Du. A small hill party was deployed to locate the pair who were assisted back down to Idwal Cottage.

Two walkers were unsure of the path whilst descending Devil's Kitchen/Twll Du so retraced their steps back up to Llyn y Cwn and called for assistance. Their location was confirmed with Sarloc and a small hill party already at base deployed to locate the pair who were then assisted back down to Idwal Cottage.

A walker lost the path in the area of Devil's Kitchen so called for help. The team leader was eventually able to locate the walker using Sarloc and a small hill team were deployed to rendezvous with the walker and assist them back to the path and down to Idwal Cottage.

A lead climber on the last pitch of Gashed Crag (South Buttress, Tryfan) fell about 10m. They were uninjured, however, their belayer suffered rope burns to both hands in the fall and was unable to continue. Due to the location the Coastguard rescue helicopter was tasked but could not access the casualty due to light winds and the number of other climbers in the vicinity. The helicopter was able to lift six team members and equipment to Caseg Fraith from where they walked up the South Ridge to an area just above the casualty party. The three climbers were brought up to the ridge using a technical rope system and then were walked off, back down to the roadside.

Two fully equipped climbers rang for advice from the 5th pitch of Grooved Arete on Tryfan. It was dark and they were not sure whether to continue up the route or to retreat. The team leader ascertained that they were competent to abseil and therefore advised that abseiling back to the Heather Terrace would be the safest option. The team were initially put on stand by but shortly afterward stood down as the climbers reported back and were making good progress. Welfare checks were carried out periodically and the climbers confirmed when they were back at their car.

Two climbers had ascended a route on the east face of Tryfan but were slowed by wet conditions and route finding. They arrived at the summit as darkness fell and, having forgotten torches, could not easily find their way off so called for help. Team members gathered at base to deploy but with deteriorating wintry conditions there was time concern for the climbers so the Coastguard helicopter was tasked. The aircraft was able to access and winch the chair from the summit area and dropped them at Oggie Base.

The Welsh Ambulance Service (WAS) requested supported with a patient who was inaccessible to them on broken ground and required possible stretcher extraction. The team began to deploy with local team members going directly to scene but the casualty party were able to extract themselves to the roadside before the team arrived.

A walker in an instructed group slipped and injured their wrist while descending Western gully on Tryfan. The group leader (Oggie TM) had assessed and strapped the arm with the intention of continuing down but requested the team be put on standby in case self-extraction was not possible. After 30 minutes the leader confirmed that team assistance would not be needed and the team were stood down.

A friend reported an overdue walker who had planned a long walk from Tal y Bont up to Foel Fras. The walker was several hours overdue in bad weather and no phone contact was possible. As the Team Leader was gathering information the walker arrived back at their car and were able to make contact so the team were stood down.

Two walkers set off to climb Tryfan by the North Ridge but got lost before they reached the summit and called for assistance as they were stuck on dangerous ground. It was likely that they had descended Notch gully and ended up in the steep terrain between V-Cleft and Y-Gully on the West Face. Due to fading daylight and their difficult position the Coastguard helicopter was requested and tasked. They managed to winch the 2 walkers from their ledge and dropped them at Oggie Base for re-warming.

Two well-equipped walkers were descending the North Ridge of Tryfan and lost the main path. One of the pair began to down-climb a steep water course but slipped and took a tumbling fall of approx 15m sustaining injuries. Their friend was unable to safely descend to them so called for assistance. Two hasty parties were deployed, one to the injured walker to assess their requirements while their friend was extracted to safe ground with a technical rope rescue (TRR) system and then taken to Oggie Base. Due to the casualty's injuries and difficult location the Coastguard helicopter was tasked but was unable to access the cas location for winch extraction. A TRR system was built and the casualty lowered in a stretcher with two attendants down to the main path. Multiple back-roped stances were established to cover the descent down to the road where the casualty was passed directly to WAST for transport to hospital.

A party of three walkers became lost while trying to descend Glyder Fach. A hill team were deployed and were able to locate the group, they were rewarmed and assisted back to the main path and off the hill.

The team were asked to assist North Wales Police in a search for a high risk missing person in an urban area. Due to a lack of suitable search areas for MR it was decided not to deploy the team until further information was available. NWP updated that the individual had been located shortly after.

A family group set out to ascend Tryfan via the west face but became separated part-way up and were unable to make contact with each other. Two of the party called for assistance and returned to the roadside in the event that the others descended. The team leader left messages and made phone enquiries until the informant called back to report that they could see the rest of their group descending from one of the west face gullies. Once safely reunited at the roadside the team leader was informed and stood the team down - no OVMRO hill deployment was required.

A group of four walkers were attempting a route up the north ridge of Tryfan but decided to turn back part way due to worsening icy conditions. While descending they lost the main footpath and became stuck in steep ground on the west face so called for assistance. A hill party was deployed and were able to locate the walkers and provided cas care to one of the party who had suffered an ankle injury before making their way to safe ground. As the injured walker was moving slowly a helicopter was requested and an aircraft from St Athan was tasked. Two team members waited with the injured walker while the remaining walkers were guided down off the hill.

Two walkers were descending the north ridge of Tryfan but lost the path and became unsure of the route, stuck on steep ground, they called for assistance. A hill party was deployed and located the walkers, they were confidence-roped down the steeper sections of the north ridge and back to base for rewarming and food before returning to their vehicle.

A party of two were attempting to scramble Bristly Ridge but became stuck near the base of the route between sinister gulley and dexter gulley. Team members already on training at base deployed directly. The team were able to access the walker's location and secure the pair before rigging a technical rope extraction. The walkers were lowered to safe ground and walked back down to Oggie base where they were re-warmed before returning to their vehicle.

A party of two were in the area of Yr Elen when one of the party injured their ankle, suffering a possible dislocation and unable to continue. Team members were preparing to deploy from base to respond to another job on Pen Yr Ole Wen so a party were readied to attend this second job but given the location and nature of the injury Rescue 936 was also requested. The helicopter was able to access the casualty and lift them directly to hospital with the remaining walker happy to descend alone. Team members were then diverted to assist the other ongoing job.

location_text: Pen yr Ole Wen, South Ridge
narrative_raw: Two walkers heard a male shout/scream as they ascended the south ridge of Pen yr Ole Wen. They descended approx 100m down the ridge to where they felt the scream originated and did a hasty search of the area and shouted, but no response. At this point they informed NWP of their concern and the team were contacted. A Team Leader spoke to the walkers and decided that no action would be taken at that time as the walkers had already searched the area. No further reports came in about shouts, and no person was reported overdue by the end of the day. False alarm with good intent.

A pair of climbers were drytooling at a quarry near Crafnant when one of them felt unwell and then collapsed. Despite attempts to resuscitate him, the casualty sadly died at the scene and was later evacuated from the quarry by the team. Welsh Ambulance Service and police attended the incident, alongside OVMRO. The thoughts of the team are with the casualty's family and friends.

An individual in the Glan Conwy area was reported as missing from home in the afternoon and categorised as high-risk. North Wales Police began initial searches and called the team for support with team members beginning deployments in the evening. Around midnight, the team was stood down with the intention of returning to assist in the morning. A call with the Police Search Advisor in the morning informed us that the person had been found, sadly deceased, outside the initial search effort.

Three walkers called 999 stating they were lost on Tryfan in the dark. As there were multiple callouts ongoing at the same time it was a few minutes before the team leader was able to make contact with the informant by which time they had found the path once more and were happy to continue down with no assistance. They confirmed by phone once they were at the roadside and no further team member deployment was required.

A solo walker on Glyder Fach slipped on snow and felt his foot go down between rocks and get trapped. He immediately rang 999 for assistance. When the Team Leader made contact with him he had managed to extract his foot and no longer needed help. He thanked the team for the speedy response and the team stood down.

A party of two walkers became stuck while descending the East side of Tryfan so called for assistance. A party of seven team members was deployed from base to locate the pair with spotters identifying the walker's location from base. The hill team were guided in to the walker's location and once with them, warmed them up and then escorted them down with some confidence roping until they were on the descent path A5.

North Wales Police asked the team to respond to a driver whose car was stuck in snow on a small lane above Betws-y-Coed. There were no welfare issues they were just stuck. Due to the severe weather conditions it would have taken a long time to access the location so the team leader advised NWP to send one of their 4x4 vehicles or contact 4x4 Response. No OVMRO deployment was required.

A couple had climbed up the southeast ridge of Siabod with the intention of descending by the north east ridge, however, once at the summit one of the pair became exhausted and unable to continue so they put up an emergency shelter and called for assistance. A quick reminder about Lake District weather…
Last week we had heat exhaustion in hot, dry conditions. This week we’re treating hypothermia in cold rain and strong winds. The Lakes can switch seasons in a matter of hours — even in June — and it catches people out every year.
Be AdventureSmart
Before you set off, ask yourself the three questions:
1️⃣ Do I have the right gear?
2️⃣ Do I know what the weather will be like?

A few minutes of planning can prevent a very long day for you — and for us.

Exhaustion, Hydration & Energy on the Fells
A fell walk of around 4 hours can burn 1,200–2,000+ calories — and longer routes burn even more.
That’s on top of your normal daily energy needs.
If you don’t replace that energy, your strength, coordination and decision‑making drop fast.
💧 In warm weather you’ll typically need 0.5–1 litre per hour — often 2–4 litres total.
A single 500 ml bottle isn’t enough.

Safety Message
We’ve seen a noticeable rise in incidents where walkers become benighted on the high fells. This isn’t about criticising anyone — plans change, people get delayed, and the mountains can be demanding.
However, a few recurring factors are worth highlighting:
- Late start times, leaving walkers short of daylight on long routes.
- No head torches, making safe navigation impossible once darkness arrives.
- Overestimating personal pace and capability, especially on big days like Scafell Pike.
Darkness is inevitable — it arrives every single day — so planning for it is essential. Choosing an appropriate start time, knowing your own pace, and carrying a working head torch for every member of the group can make all the difference.
The fells are incredible places. A little preparation helps ensure everyone enjoys them safely and gets home under their own steam.
